transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… I know elevators aren’t really dangerous, but when I have to get in one, I get really scared. It feels like I’m going to be trapped in there, and I just can’t make myself feel normal about it.
Do you ever have episodes where you feel an intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes?
Yes. It happens fast, like right when the elevator doors start closing. My chest gets tight, my hands get sweaty, and I just keep thinking, I need to get out, even if it’s only a couple floors.
Do you experience this kind of fear in situations other than being in elevators?
Not really. I mean, I get stressed like anybody, but that scared feeling like that mostly happens with elevators.
Is your fear of elevators related to the enclosed space itself or something else about the elevator?

It’s more the feeling of being trapped, I think. Like, I know the elevator probably isn’t dangerous, but once I’m in there I get scared I won’t be able to get out, and I can’t calm myself down like I should.
Do you find yourself avoiding elevators or situations where you might need to use an elevator because of your fear?

Yeah, I do. Most days I’ll take the stairs, at my apartment and at job sites too. If an elevator or one of those lifts is the only way up, I try to ask for different work if I can. If I really have to ride it, I need someone I trust right there with me.
Do you ever feel trapped or scared in other small or enclosed spaces, like cars or rooms?
I don’t think so. Cars and rooms don’t really bother me like that. It’s mostly elevators where I get that trapped feeling.
Have you ever had an episode of intense fear or discomfort like the one you described in the elevator, but in a situation where you weren't in an elevator?
No, not really. I can’t think of a time I felt that same kind of intense fear unless I was in an elevator or dealing with having to get in one.
Do you worry about having another episode of intense fear like the ones you have in elevators in other aspects of your life?
Not really, no. I don’t sit around worrying it’s gonna happen in other parts of my life. It’s more just when I know I might have to deal with an elevator.
Has your fear of elevators significantly impacted your daily life or relationships?

Yeah, some. I still get to work and my GED class, but I’ll take the stairs even when it’s a lot, so I end up late or worn out. And on construction jobs, if it’s something where I’d have to use an elevator, I’ve turned those down, so that makes me less useful sometimes.
Do you think you're scared of the elevator itself or of having one of those intense fear episodes while you're in the elevator?

I think it’s the elevator itself, mostly. I know in my head it’s probably not actually dangerous, but when I have to get in one, I get scared I’m gonna be trapped in there. Then I just can’t make myself feel normal about it.
Is your fear of elevators because you're worried about having one of those intense fear episodes, like a panic attack, while you're in the elevator?

Not exactly. It’s more the elevator itself. I know it’s not really dangerous, but when I have to get in one, I start feeling like I’m going to get trapped in there, and I just can’t make myself feel normal about it.
Is there something specific about elevators that triggers your fear, or is it more about the situation of being in an elevator?

It’s more being in the elevator, I think. Like, I know it’s not really dangerous, but once I have to get in, I start feeling like I’m going to be trapped in there, and I can’t get myself to feel okay about it.
Is your fear of elevators triggered by something specific that happens when you are in the elevator, like the doors closing or the movement, or is it just being in the elevator in general?

It’s mostly when the doors start closing. As soon as they slide shut, my chest gets tight, my hands get sweaty, and I just start thinking, I need to get out of here. Even if it’s only a couple floors, that feeling hits right away.
Do you think you would feel scared or trapped if you were in a situation that felt similar to an elevator, but wasn't actually an elevator?

Yeah, I think it would be the same kind of thing if it felt like I couldn’t get out. It’s not that I think elevators are actually dangerous, but when I’m in one, I feel trapped and scared, and I just can’t make myself calm down about it.
Would you feel scared or trapped in a situation that is not an elevator but has a similar feeling of being enclosed or restricted?

Yeah, if it had that same feeling where I couldn’t really get out, I think I’d feel scared. It’s not that I believe it’s actually dangerous, but once I feel trapped like that, I just can’t make myself feel normal about it.
Would your fear of being trapped decrease if you were in a very large enclosed space?

Probably, yeah. If it was a big enclosed space, I don’t think it would hit me the same way. It’s really when I’m in an elevator and the doors close that I get scared, like I’m trapped and can’t make myself feel normal, even though I know it’s not actually dangerous.
Would you feel scared or trapped in other small, enclosed spaces like a small room with no windows?

I think it could, if it had that same feeling of being stuck. For me it’s really elevators—when the doors close, I know it’s not actually dangerous, but I get scared like I’m trapped and I can’t make myself feel normal.
Would your fear of being trapped occur in any other enclosed space besides an elevator?

Not really that I’ve noticed. It’s mostly elevators for me. I know they’re not actually dangerous, but once I have to get in one and the doors close, I get scared like I’m going to be trapped and I can’t get myself to feel normal.
Would you feel scared or trapped in any situation where you feel confined or restricted, regardless of whether it's an elevator or not?

It’s really the elevator part for me. Like, I know it’s not actually dangerous, but when I have to get in and the doors close, I get scared like I’m going to be trapped in there, and I can’t make myself feel normal about it.
